text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Prod us-west streaming decode p99 spike detected (3.4x baseline). Symptoms: streaming stalls, partial responses, increased paging. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-latency>.

mara: seeing it on dashboards. p95 up ~1.6x, p99 brutal. Any recent infra/kernel changes deployed to us-west?

samir: quick metrics: p95 = 420ms -> 680ms, p99 = 820ms -> 2800ms on streaming cluster (gpu-pool-stream-03). Error rate for chunked responses +3.2%.

jing: logs show lots of KV cache misses around same time, and a surge of pagefaults in decode path. Stack traces point to compilepath variant "trt8-flashattn-v2" on nodes returning tail stalls.

devops-bot: recent rollout note: kernel compile pipeline rolled trt8-flashattn-v2 to canary in us-west at 2026-03-15T02:12Z, finished grad rollout at 02:40Z. See deploy: ci/builds/7864.

mara: okay suspicious. samir can you correlate the spike start time with the completed rollout window?

samir: yes, spike onset ~02:45Z, aligns with rollout completion +5min. Strong correlation.

jing: repro on staging when switching to the v2 kernel: reproduce streaming stall after ~30s of sustained traffic. Heap traces + nvprof show decode kernel falling back to slower path because of misaligned kernel selection.

jing: potential culprit: new compiler flag "-fassume-fast-attn" enabled in the build that changes kernel selection heuristics for long prefix sequences.

mara: can we rollforward a patch quickly (recompile without the flag) or rollback the kernel variant? Which is faster?

devops-bot: rollback of variant to previous tag (trt8-flashattn-v1) can be done via infra tag rollback, should be ~12m to roll across us-west. Rebuild without flag is ~18-25m plus canary.

jing: patch idea: rebuild with fallback guard (ATTN_FALLBACK=1) to force older kernel for sequences >1024. Quick patch and hotreplace is possible.

samir: mitigation plan proposal: 1) immediate: route streaming traffic for p95/p99-sensitive routes to fallback model variant (quantized-runtime-small) to reduce pressure; 2) mid: rollback kernel variant to v1; 3) post: rebuild without -fassume-fast-attn and run extended perf tests.

mara: agree. execute step 1 now. Lia, can you notify CS about potential customer latency impact and ask them to throttle non-critical jobs?

lia: on it. I'll open a short status note and ping top 5 affected customers (PocketHealth, Formsly, NotesPro).

mara: ops commands:

```
# pin streaming route to fallback model for low-latency streams
redwoodctl route set --route streaming --model gpt-stream-quant:v1 --selector region=us-west --force
# increase dedicated pool for streaming for 30m
redwoodctl capacity adjust --pool gpu-pool-stream-03 --delta +2 --duration 30m
```

samir: running the route pin now.

deploy-bot: route set accepted. Canary rollout to 10% within 60s.

samir: canary metrics: p99 on canary route dropped to ~720ms within 90s. Good signal. Pushing to 100% for affected routes now.

mara: while that propagates, start rollback of kernel variant to v1. devops-bot you said ~12m? Please kick it off and share progress.

devops-bot: starting rollback: infra orchestrator job 9921 queued -> executing. Will update on each region.

incidents-bot: page assigned to oncall-escalation: mara, samir. Severity: SEV2. Start time: 2026-03-15T02:46Z.

jing: for engineering postmortem: gather flamegraphs, nvprof traces, and the compile flags matrix. Current suspect flags: [-O3 -march=sm90 -flto -fassume-fast-attn]. We'll diff kernel trace with v1.

samir: rollback completed in us-west at 02:58Z. Verified variant is trt8-flashattn-v1 on all nodes.

mara: re-run metrics: p99 back down to ~780ms across streaming routes, p95 ~430ms. Still slightly above baseline but much better.

jing: staging confirm: v1 doesn't trigger the slow fallback path. Looks like the heuristic change in v2 is the root.

mara: next steps: 1) keep route pinned until we have a clean rebuild; 2) schedule a rebuild without -fassume-fast-attn and run a longer stress test (24h heavy streaming); 3) add an emergency canary test that runs sequence-length distributions to catch heuristic regressions.

lia: CS update posted. Customers informed about degraded performance window and that we are rolling back a kernel variant. SLA risk flagged for a handful of customers but no full outage.

oncall-ian: I'll take handoff at 03:15Z. What do you want me to watch?

mara: watch p99 <900ms for 1h and error rate for partial streams <0.5%. If metrics hold, de-escalate and close. Also confirm rollback stays stable after autoscaler events.

samir: I've captured traces and uploaded to internal share: <https://redwood.internal/artifacts/streaming-spike/4512345679>. Jing will lead the root-cause.

jing: assigning follow-ups: (1) perf/regression: disable -fassume-fast-attn by default until we have a safe heuristic (owner: jing), (2) infra: add pre-rollout canary that runs streaming sequences on family of hardware (owner: devops), (3) product: add alert for KV cache miss rate spike (owner: mara).

mara: copy. I'll file the incident ticket and link artifacts.

incidents-bot: SEV2 incident status updated -> mitigated (routing pin + rollback). Keep monitoring for 60m.

oncall-ian: ack, taking over. I'll escalate to oncall-manager if p99 > 1s for next 15m.

mara: thanks team. Good triage and fast rollback. We'll write a short postmortem and schedule the rebuild behind a stricter canary. :thumbsup:

lia: leaving a customer follow-up note for PocketHealth support ticket #PH-2209.

text-note: end of thread — handoff complete.
